summary: On the main deck, a diagram appears on the screen. Tank says he has it. Morpheus, heard only as a voice over, then demands the main wet-wall.

what_changes.before: Working to locate the requested structural drawing
what_changes.evidence: The diagram windows onto the screen. TANK Got it.

what_changes.before: Waiting for Tank to find a structural drawing
what_changes.after: Directs the next requirement, the main wet-wall
what_changes.evidence: MORPHEUS (V.O.) I need the main wet-wall.

event_hint.one_line: Morpheus guides Tank through the building's schematics as the crew tries to find a way out.

minds.wants: To deliver the exact structural data Morpheus needs, fast enough to matter while the crew is being hunted.
minds.feels: A taut, channeled urgency — fear for the crew he cannot physically reach converted into the one thing he can do: keep the schematic flowing ahead of Morpheus's needs. He is the crew's eyes now, and the pressure of that is total.
minds.shows: A clipped, functional "Got it" — confirmation without a trace of panic, the voice of a calm operator rather than a frightened friend.
minds.basis: sc-104 has Tank answer the call and get ordered to "find a structural drawing of this building and find it fast." Here the diagram "windows onto the screen" and he says "Got it," then Morpheus immediately demands the next item — the exchange is a rapid request/fulfillment loop, not a conversation. The event shape (crew trapped, boot-steps closing, Mouse just killed) supplies the stakes Tank is holding back.

believes_about.belief: That Morpheus has a plan and that feeding him the building's schematics in sequence is what will get the crew out.
believes_about.wrong_because: Tank does not yet know Morpheus's plan is to sacrifice himself — that Morpheus will hold Smith down and be captured, which Tank will soon realize is a trap. The competence-loop they are in masks that this is a rearguard action, not an escape.

minds.wants: To keep the crew moving through the building by naming the next structural element before they are cornered.
minds.feels: Barely-contained desperation under absolute command. He is guiding an escape in real time while knowing the Agents are closing and that every second of hesitation could get them killed — the weight of their lives is on his instructions.
minds.shows: Only a voice, and only a demand: "I need the main wet-wall." No greeting, no reassurance, no emotion — pure directive, the tone of a man who has no time to be anything but efficient.
minds.basis: In sc-103 he seized the phone and overrode Trinity's objection ("We have no choice") to keep the line open; here he continues sc-104's order to locate the building's structure, now pushing Tank from the general drawing to the specific wet-wall. The V.O. framing and the imperative phrasing show a leader driving the escape from a distance, with the firefight/trap of the event bearing down.

believes_about.belief: That Tank can keep pace — that the operator on the ship can pull each schematic as fast as Morpheus calls for it.
believes_about.wrong_because: A working belief under pressure rather than a dramatic error: it holds here (Tank delivers instantly), but it depends on Tank maintaining that speed while the situation degrades toward Morpheus's capture.

connects_back: sc-104: Tank answering the call and being ordered to find a structural drawing fast — this scene is the fulfillment of that order.
sc-103: Morpheus taking the phone ("We have no choice") and overriding Trinity's tracking concern, establishing the remote-guided escape this exchange serves.
The event (Mouse's death, bricked windows, closing Agents): the urgency and stakes that turn a technical exchange into a life-or-death relay.
sets_up: Morpheus guiding the crew through the building's internal plumbing/wet-walls to escape, which his demand for the main wet-wall initiates.
The rearguard action in which Morpheus holds Smith down and is captured — the competent escape-loop this scene depicts is the prelude to that loss.
Tank's role as the ship's eyes during the escape, positioning his later realization ("it's a trap") and his survival of Cypher's betrayal in ev-023.
dramatic_function: To compress a life-or-death escape into a terse technical relay, letting the audience feel the crew's dependence on coordination under pursuit while denying any emotional release — the scene keeps momentum taut and keeps Morpheus as an off-screen commanding presence right before his imminent capture.
